lines.speaker: Knemon
lines.text: This is that proverb: the fawn taking on the lion.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Why are you so upset, Knemon?

lines.speaker: Knemon
lines.text: You ask why I'm upset? I left an unwilling heir after being outsmarted, the wretch that I am, and skipped over the people I most wanted to have my things.

lines.speaker: Knemon
lines.text: I was looking after Hermolaus, the very rich childless man, hoping for his death. He didn't dislike the attention. It seemed clever to me to make an open will leaving him all my property, so that he might envy me and do the same.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: So what did he do then?

lines.speaker: Knemon
lines.text: I don't know what he wrote in his own will, but I suddenly died when the roof fell on me. And now Hermolaus has my things like a sea bass that swallowed the hook along with the bait.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Not only that, but you the fisherman too. So you've devised a scheme against yourself.

lines.speaker: Knemon
lines.text: It seems so. That's why I'm the one groaning now.
